teaser: Why investors pick one founder over another who looks just as good: coachability, contracts that move control, and who the commodity is.
core_idea: We study survivors, so the question is why one founder was chosen over another who did the same; the hypothesis is that investors select partly for control, moving the founder towards commodity as labels did to performers; investors prefer coachable founders though coachability does not reliably predict success, contracts hand control to investors when performance is poor and make leaving expensive, and half of founders were replaced by year three; founder control lowers valuations, but over the long run founder-led companies returned more, and the hypothesis can be tested.

quotes.text: Coachability is a polite word for it. Controllability is a less polite one.
Replaceability is not an accident of venture capital; it is designed in.
It is to get to the big stick before you need their money
